title: The Intellectual Type
text: “Nap time can wait for later. Please set the luggage down here.”
“Okay.”
And so Father set down the overnight bag he’d brought with him, indeed.
“What should we do now? Should everyone just gather and wait around? Isn’t there some welcome thing Wolf planned for here?”
“Wolf already told the servants and the nearby nobles, and preparations are underway. There’s a fair bit of free time. I can show you around anywhere.”
Is there anywhere you’d like to go? Wolf asked Father, indeed.
“Hmm, let’s see… Given what we were just talking about, maybe I’ll take a look at your room, Wolf.”
“Woof! You’re curious about my room?”
Wolf asked, eyes sparkling.
“It’s a home visit, after all. If you don’t want me to see it, I won’t go, though?”
“I want you to see it!”
“Oh, is that so?”
While they were exchanging words like that, my usaunny ears caught Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy starting to whisper to each other, indeed.
“Having his own room be the first place he shows someone—whether he realizes it or not, it’s a bit of a problem, isn’t it?”
“Indeed.”
“Still, on my end, I asked around the mansion about where I used to live and went to see it myself. I wanted to be considerate, in case there were any memories left, even a little.”

“It’s the kind of attitude that invites misunderstanding, but he really doesn’t realize it. Now that you mention it, I went along to see what used to be my own room too. I asked Eclair-sama and Elmelo to prioritize the repairs.”

Incidentally, in Big Sister’s case, her home was already gone, so there was an occasion where she and Father went to see the site together, indeed. The consideration shown was the same regardless, indeed. And so, it seemed the place they were now headed to was what used to be Wolf’s room, indeed.
“Here.”
“Ohh, Wolf’s room…”
With a click, they opened the door to Wolf’s room, and inside were a great many bookshelves, indeed.
“Ohh… so it’s a study? Nothing but books.”
“Woof. Loves reading.”
“You don’t do any reading these days at all, though.”
“I do, though?”
Wolf tilted his head slightly, objecting to Rabbit Guy’s words, indeed.
“You sometimes put on glasses and read one-handed, don’t you? Kind of gives off that ‘sturdy-bodied wolfman who still studies’ vibe.”
“Woof.”
“All I remember is you running around as a peckul on Cal Mira Island, having the time of your life.”
“Grrr.”
Wolf let out a growl of intimidation, indeed.
“Well, it’s kind of like Theo’s room lately, isn’t it? You two seem similar enough that you could probably find common ground to talk about.”
“The language I’m studying makes it a bit hard to read, honestly. If it’s translated, maybe I can manage somehow.”

Rabbit Guy only knew a little of Shieldfreeden’s language and writing—everything else was within the range he’d studied together with Father, indeed. Wolf, on the other hand, had already become a Hero, so language wasn’t an issue for him; it seemed his writing was mainly oriented toward Siltvelt, indeed.
“It’s got that feel of foreign books lined up. Hard to read.”
Crocodile Guy was from Melromarc, so his reading and writing were based on Melromarc standards, indeed. In that respect, he was the same as Big Sister, indeed.
“I can read it, I say.”
Having been in this world for so many years, I could read almost anything, indeed.
“Why are you competing over this?”
“There’s stuff like reading the same story in translation, right? That kind of talk seems like it’d get Wolf and Theo pretty fired up.”
“This guy usually goofs around about as much as Spear Hero does, so he doesn’t get into that kind of deep literary discussion.”
“Woof—if you throw Rishia into the mix, it’ll definitely get lively.”
“I won’t deny that. That person is genuinely sharp.”

Riska, was it? Indeed, apparently she was actually in the top ranks academically at the Faubrey school. That she didn’t stand out much was likely just her own temperament. Since it was also the location of the rather accomplished Filo-tan fan club, I could recall that much, indeed.
“Thinking about it again, it’s kind of wild how many high-IQ acquaintances we have—but anyway, so this is what Wolf’s room looks like. Oh, there’s even something like an iron dumbbell here.”
“It’s partly our family motto, and partly that my brother was all brawn, so between assisting him and being his sparring partner all the time…”
Just so, Wolf’s tone seemed to dip ever so slightly when talking about his brother, indeed.
“You’re totally in the ‘hard-working underling’ position, but you don’t give off that vibe at all, Wolf.”
“Heh heh.”
What was he smiling so suggestively about, I wondered?
“You honestly seem like the intellectual type, though. Just looking at this room, anyway.”
“There’s no trace of that left in him now.”
“Woof.”
Wolf scratched his head, looking a little embarrassed, indeed.
“That wasn’t a compliment.”
“Did you actually go to school and stuff, Wolf? Seems like something a noble would do.”
“Yeah. Went for a while. Though once I started serving as my brother’s attendant, it was mostly self-study and lessons from a tutor who came by.”
“You two got along well, huh, you and your brother.”
At Father’s words, Wolf’s face seemed to grow a little lonely for a moment, but he nodded right away, indeed.
“Woof! He was a dumb brother, but there was nothing two-faced about him, so he was easy to get along with.”
“If anything, I hear it was you who was in the two-faced position, wasn’t it?”
“That’s right.”
“I think it’s a good thing, brothers getting along well, don’t you?”
“Father has a younger brother too, doesn’t he, indeed?”
“That’s right.”
Father didn’t talk about it much, but apparently he had an accomplished younger brother, indeed. There was also talk about him being concerned with appearances, indeed.
“I’m a little curious about Iwatani-sama’s younger brother.”

“I talk about him sometimes—he’s got that concern-with-appearances streak, but he’s a good student, sports and studies both. Meanwhile, my grades were worse compared to his. I used to get called the ‘useless one’ of the Iwatani brothers.”

He said it so casually, but… I found myself more curious about what kind of monster this younger brother must be, to have abilities surpassing even Father, indeed. From the way Itsuki talked about it too, he suspected Father might just be a doting older brother spoiling his little brother rotten. My own read on it… was that the brother probably only excelled academically, and lost to Father in everything else—something like that kind of status, wouldn’t you say?
“It’s a common thing everywhere, really, a younger brother being more accomplished than the older one. Even with athletes, there’s talk of the younger sibling performing better.”
“Is that how it is, I wonder.”
“Theo found his cousin too, and Shion’s got Eclair-san, right? That kind of relationship is nice, isn’t it.”
“…Naofumi-sama, do you want to see your brother again?”

Wolf asked, seeming somewhat hesitant, indeed. My guess was that Father’s answer probably wasn’t going to be all that enthusiastic. After all, even in the other loops, he never once said anything like wanting to see his brother, indeed.

“My brother’s probably fine without me around. I did kind of look down on him a bit, and now that you mention it, he told me to make stew that night, didn’t he. Ha, guess I never got to make it for him.”

Father laughed with a faintly self-mocking edge, indeed. It was the reaction of someone who’d come to another world and simply didn’t know what had happened since. To begin with… this was one of the looping worlds, so according to the Spear Spirit, wasn’t there supposed to be no connection to other worlds? The Father of the very first world had mentioned once that he’d returned home, so perhaps various things had happened around that time. More than anything, he hadn’t shown any sign of worry about that at all, indeed. And… now that I thought back to when I began the loop, it seemed the Father of that very first world had somehow managed to reunite with Filo-tan, so he was likely still alive even now. Surely things with his younger brother had been resolved well too. Oh? Now that I thought of it, hadn’t I heard something about Tiger Guy being called over to that world’s Father, to scold Tiger Girl after she’d gone over there? And Father being split into multiple instances, or something like that…? How did that go again? Was it alright to talk about it? Perhaps better to hold off. It was all vague and unconfirmed, so I’d keep quiet about it, indeed.
“Woof.”
After a brief silence following Father’s answer, Wolf let out a small cry, as if in agreement, indeed.
